original_question: For which dimensions 2n − 1 and orders q of the fundamental group is every lens space of volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q spectrally unique within the class of lens spaces with that same dimension and group order, so that no nontrivial isospectrality occurs?
target_in_paper: §8.3, Problem 8.7, with its immediate setup in equation (54) and its motivation from Conjecture 8.6 in equation (55).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s target as an odd-dimensional lens-space question parameterized by n and q, restricted to lens spaces with cyclic fundamental group of order q and therefore volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q, and it correctly asks for the regime in which no non-isometric isospectrality occurs inside that fixed dimension/order class.
missing_details: The paper quantifies n and q as positive integers and works with (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces endowed with the standard constant-sectional-curvature-one metric.
The comparison class is not all parameter tuples (q; s), but the set 𝔏(n, q) of isometry classes of (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order q.
The exact meaning of “spectrally unique” is uniqueness with respect to the full Laplace–Beltrami spectrum Spec(L), counted with multiplicity.
The paper formalizes the condition as 𝔏•(n, q) = 𝔏(n, q), where 𝔏•(n, q) = {L in 𝔏(n, q) : Spec(L') ≠ Spec(L) for every L' ≠ L in 𝔏(n, q)}.
“No nontrivial isospectrality” should be phrased as “no non-isometric pair in 𝔏(n, q) is isospectral,” because 𝔏(n, q) already consists of isometry classes.

The equivalence between “fundamental group of order q” and “volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q” depends on the quotient-volume formula vol(S^d/Γ) = vol(S^d)/|Γ| together with the lens-space model L(q; s) = S^(2n−1)/Γ_{q; s}, where |Γ_{q; s}| = q.

The surrounding motivation is that Problem 8.7 is proposed as a first step toward Conjecture 8.6, which predicts that, for fixed n, spectrally unique lens spaces have asymptotic density 1 among all lens spaces as q grows.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the missing stand-alone data are geometric: the metric normalization, the operator whose spectrum is used, and the isometry-class quantifiers.
refined_question: For positive integers n and q, let 𝔏(n, q) denote the set of isometry classes of (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces with cyclic fundamental group of order q, endowed with the standard constant-curvature-one metric, and let 𝔏•(n, q) = {L in 𝔏(n, q) : Spec(L') ≠ Spec(L) for every L' ≠ L in 𝔏(n, q)}, where Spec denotes the Laplace–Beltrami spectrum counted with multiplicity. Determine conditions on n and q for which 𝔏•(n, q) = 𝔏(n, q).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for which positive integers n and q is no non-isometric Laplace-isospectral pair possible among (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces of volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q?
justification: The draft clearly targets a different part of the paper than the earlier theorems: it matches the official open problem in §8.3, Problem 8.7, not Theorem 1.3. The paper first asks in Problem 8.5 whether a “generic” lens space is spectrally unique, then defines 𝔏(n, q) and 𝔏•(n, q) in equation (54), introduces the density 𝒰_n(x) in equation (55), states Conjecture 8.6 that lim_{x→∞} 𝒰_n(x) = 1, and immediately presents Problem 8.7 as a first step toward that conjecture. Your wording already captures the core content of Problem 8.7, but to be fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper it must specify the set-theoretic formulation 𝔏•(n, q) = 𝔏(n, q), the fact that the comparison is among isometry classes, and that “spectrum” means the full Laplace–Beltrami spectrum counted with multiplicity. The volume clause in your draft is faithful, but it implicitly uses the quotient formula vol(S^d/Γ) = vol(S^d)/|Γ| together with the standard lens-space realization L(q; s) = S^(2n−1)/Γ_{q; s}.
